title: zero-point-kernel (v0.5.0)
description: A small x86-64 research kernel written in Rust, no_std, that boots under QEMU and on real hardware, and that runs every state-changing request past a policy gate before carrying it out. Each decision is appended to a linked log; the link detects accidental corruption and is not tamper-evident against anyone who can write the file. The private policy engine is not included, and a demo policy stands in its place, so a build from this source runs programs and the gate can be observed working. The package contains the kernel (zpl-kernel), its bare-metal binary (zpl-kernel-bin), a Limine bridge for booting from an ISO (limine-bridge), a small assembler (zpl-asm), a filesystem format and image tool (zpl-fs, zpl-mkfs), a log replay tool (audit-replay), and a QEMU test runner (zpl-test-runner). It is a research kernel: not a general-purpose operating system, and nothing important should run on it.
notes: Uploading this is a separate decision from preparing it. Nothing in this repository has been published.
